title: Introduce credential warmup + compact StreamHandle adapter and unify backoff config names
author: Jordan Li
release_notes: Added StreamHandle abstraction and credential warmup window; unified backoff option names across SDKs; bump TypeScript SDK to v1.7.0. No breaking changes for existing call sites but some internal config keys are aliased.
description: Context: Several production incidents showed transient mid-stream auth refresh races and inconsistent backoff naming between SDKs. This PR implements a compact TypeScript-only StreamHandle adapter plus a credential ‘warmup’ window that proactively refreshes short-lived tokens before they expire to avoid mid-stream failures. The change also renames internal backoff config keys to match the cross-SDK spec (backoffBaseMs -> baseBackoffMs, backoffFactor -> multiplier) and provides backwards-compatible aliases to avoid breaking users. Motivation: parity with Go/Python ergonomics, reduce tail latency spikes caused by token refresh, and centralize telemetry for stream stalls. Summary of changes: - Add StreamHandle abstraction (lightweight wrapper around native stream iterator) that exposes pause/resume, a normalized 'onStall' hook, and a lease-friendly attach/detach API. - Implement credential warmup: SDK now accepts credentialWarmupSeconds (default 8s) that triggers a refresh flow N seconds before expiry when a stream is active. Works with rotating token providers and fallback chains. - Normalize backoff config names to the cross-SDK spec; add compatibility layer for older keys and log a single notice for the first-run migration. - Add telemetry hooks: stream.stall_ms histogram, stream.cred_refresh_count, and stream.warmup_trigger boolean. - Unit + integration tests: added 42 unit tests, an end-to-end scenario that runs against a local mock server and a simulated rotating-cred provider. - Examples and docs: updated streaming quickstart and migration notes. Commits (high level): - Add StreamHandle and tests - Credential warmup implementation and telemetry - Backoff key normalization + aliases - Examples and changelog + version bump - Polish, address review feedback Changed files (high level): - src/stream/StreamHandle.ts - src/auth/credentialWarmup.ts - src/config/backoffNormalization.ts - src/telemetry/streamMetrics.ts - examples/streaming-warmup.md - test/unit/stream-warmup.test.ts - package.json (version -> 1.7.0) - docs/migration/stream-warmup.md Review conversation summary: - Samir: requested stronger invariants around concurrent refreshes and suggested using a single-flight dedupe for warmup requests. - Author (Jordan): implemented single-flight dedupe in credentialWarmup.ts and added unit tests that assert only one refresh happens for concurrent stall triggers. - Katherine: asked for clarifying API docs and an example showing legacy config keys; author added examples/ + migration notes. - Luca: asked for a perf microbenchmark; author added a small benchmark in test/e2e/bench-warmup.ts and included results in the PR description: warmup adds <0.2ms median per-token overhead and eliminates a 98th-percentile stall seen in the previous harness. CI & merging: - Initial CI run: 2 flaky tests failed (test/network-failure-sim and test/stream-reconnect-unstable) — suspected unrelated flakiness. - Reran CI after test stabilization; all checks passed (unit, lint, build, e2e with mock server). - Merge method: squash and merge. Post-merge actions: - Cut SDK release v1.7.0 and publish changelog. - Notify SDK slack channel and tag Python/Go SDK owners to align naming (they already have matching aliases in their branches). Backwards compatibility notes: - Old backoff config keys are still supported via aliasing layer but will warn once on first use. - credentialWarmupSeconds defaults to 8s; existing users will not see behavioral change unless they opt-in to a non-default token provider.
